attribution_limitations: Table 1 lists separate rows at 9, 12 and 15 years, while the narrative describes interventions "Between 7 and 15 years of age". The source does not say that table-row events and narrative events are the same, so both are kept separately and not merged.

Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is described only as "considered unlikely", unlike Klippel-Trenaunay and Maffucci syndromes which are "excluded"; it is recorded as a hedged differential, not as refuted.

The time of the BRBNS diagnosis is not stated in its own sentence; it rests "on the basis of" postoperative pathological findings, which is basis wording and does not order the diagnosis after the 7-year resection. No age and no order relation are assigned to the diagnosis.
The text calls the early skin lesions pale-blue masses first noted at 18 months, while Table 1 calls the same row venous malformations; both wordings are quoted.
Detailed records of some previous interventions at outside institutions were unavailable, so earlier timing, procedures and extent are limited to what the text and Table 1 print.

The sentence reporting no recurrent melena or hematochezia, no further transfusion requirement, no treatment-related complication and continued oral iron does not itself name the follow-up assessments, so the "2 weeks, 1 month, and 2 months after discharge" of the preceding sentence is not assigned to those facts; they remain linked to the follow-up event. Supplementary Data sheet 1 prints per-visit statements for these items.

Between 7 and 15 years the text says he "required" multiple blood transfusions, which alone does not establish that they were given (action unknown); Table 1 (15 years) and the Table 2 present-case row ("repeated prior transfusions") state transfusions that were given, recorded separately.

The excision of superficial and soft-tissue masses is stated in the 7-to-15-year paragraph but its own sentence gives no time ("also"); it is left untimed and is not merged with the 15-year excision of superficial lesions in Table 1.
